name: Burp Suite Community/Pro
purpose: Integrated platform for intercepting, replaying, scanning, and analyzing web traffic.
arch: Java-based proxy with Proxy, Repeater, Intruder, Scanner (Pro), Sequencer, Decoder, Comparer, Logger; Collaborator for OOB detection.
install: Download from https://portswigger.net/burp; Community is free, Pro licensed.
cmd: Set browser proxy to 127.0.0.1:8080; install CA cert; use Proxy -> Repeater; right-click -> Send to Repeater.
advanced: Extensions (BApp Store), macros/session handling, Collaborator, active/passive scan policy tuning.
output: HTTP history with request/response; issues with confidence/severity; scanner findings.
example: Intercept a login in a lab, send to Repeater, change a parameter, observe response differences.
mistakes: Scanning out-of-scope hosts; not installing CA cert (HTTPS unreadable); trusting scanner results blindly.
limits: Community lacks active scanner and speed; steep UI learning curve.

name: OWASP ZAP
purpose: Free, open-source web application security scanner and intercepting proxy.
arch: Java proxy with passive/active scanning, spider, fuzzer, AJAX spider, and API; HUD mode.
install: Download from https://www.zaproxy.org/download/ or install via package manager.
cmd: Set proxy 127.0.0.1:8080; quick start or automated scan; use Spider then Active Scan on a lab.
advanced: ZAP API for CI, scripts (Zest, JS), authentication support, context/scope definitions.
output: Sites tree, Alerts tab with risk levels and CWE mappings, request/response views.
example: Run an automated scan against OWASP Juice Shop in a local Docker lab and review alerts.
mistakes: Scanning without scope; ignoring false positives; using aggressive scan on production.
limits: Noisy active scan; can disrupt apps; slower than commercial tools.

name: Caido
purpose: Modern web security auditing toolkit with an intercepting proxy and workflow automation.
arch: Rust-based proxy with a web UI, intercept, replay, search, and a package ecosystem.
install: Download from https://caido.io/ (free and Pro tiers).
cmd: Configure browser proxy; import CA cert; use Match/Replace rules and Replay.
advanced: Workflows (visual automation), plugins, project sharing, large request search.
output: Traffic table with search/filter, replay results, issue tracking.
example: Filter traffic by host in a lab and replay a modified request.
mistakes: Assuming feature parity with Burp; missing CA cert setup.
limits: Newer ecosystem; fewer extensions than Burp.

name: mitmproxy
purpose: Interactive, scriptable HTTP/HTTPS intercepting proxy.
arch: Python-based console proxy (mitmproxy), CLI (mitmdump), and web UI (mitmweb); scripting API.
install: pip install mitmproxy or see https://mitmproxy.org/.
cmd: mitmproxy -p 8080; set browser proxy; install mitmproxy CA cert.
advanced: Python addons to modify traffic automatically; reverse-proxy and upstream modes.
output: Interactive flow list, request/response detail, script output.
example: Write a small addon that adds a header to every request in a lab.
mistakes: Forgetting CA cert; running scripts against unintended traffic.
limits: Console UI less beginner-friendly; no active scanner.

name: Postman
purpose: API development and testing client for crafting and organizing requests.
arch: Electron app with request builder, collections, environments, scripts, and mock servers.
cmd: Create a request, set method/URL/headers/body, add environment variables, send.
advanced: Pre-request/test scripts, collections as code, Newman CLI for CI.
output: Response body, status, time, headers; test results tab.
example: Build a collection of lab API requests with an auth token variable.
mistakes: Storing real secrets in collections; sending requests to wrong environment.
limits: Not a security scanner; manual testing tool.

name: Insomnia
purpose: Lightweight API client with a focus on REST, GraphQL, and gRPC.
arch: Electron app with workspaces, environments, and plugin support.
cmd: Create request, set auth (Bearer/Basic), send; use environment variables.
advanced: GraphQL query editor, gRPC support, code generation.
output: Formatted responses by content type; history.
example: Test a lab GraphQL endpoint with introspection and a custom query.
mistakes: Leaving debug tokens in workspace files.
limits: Smaller ecosystem than Postman.

name: HTTP Toolkit
purpose: HTTP(S) debugging and interception toolkit with a polished desktop UI.
arch: Electron desktop app with a local proxy, mock/rewrite rules, and request inspection.
cmd: Launch browser via toolkit; inspect HTTPS requests; add breakpoints/rewrite rules.
advanced: On-demand mocking, HTTPS interception for mobile via proxy settings.
output: Request list with bodies, timing, and rewrite results.
example: Intercept a lab app's API call and rewrite a response to test client behavior.
mistakes: Cert trust setup on mobile devices.
limits: Not focused on vulnerability scanning.

name: Wireshark
purpose: Graphical network protocol analyzer for deep packet inspection.
arch: Qt GUI with libpcap capture engine and protocol dissectors; display filters.
cmd: Select interface; start capture; use display filter http or dns; follow TCP stream.
advanced: Capture filters (BPF), display filters, statistics, decryption of TLS with keys, Lua plugins.
output: Packet list, details pane, raw bytes; colored conversations.
example: Capture a TCP handshake to a site you own and inspect SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK.
mistakes: Capturing without permission on shared networks; ignoring sensitive data in captures.
limits: Large captures consume disk; TLS decryption requires keys.

name: tcpdump
purpose: Command-line packet capture and filtering tool.
arch: C library libpcap with Berkeley Packet Filter syntax; CLI output or pcap files.
cmd: tcpdump -i any -nn 'tcp port 80'; tcpdump -w cap.pcap 'icmp'.
advanced: BPF filters, -A/-X for payload/hex, ring buffers, reading pcap files with -r.
output: Line-per-packet text with timestamps, IPs, ports, flags.
example: Capture DNS queries from your machine and identify resolver IPs.
mistakes: Capturing on interfaces you do not own; missing -nn causes slow DNS lookups.
limits: No protocol dissection like Wireshark; text output is terse.

name: Nmap
purpose: Network discovery and security auditing scanner.
arch: C/C++ scanner with host discovery, port scan techniques, version/OS detection, NSE scripting.
cmd: nmap -sV -sC -oA out target  (authorized targets only).
advanced: NSE scripts, -A aggressive, timing templates (-T0..-T5), IPv6 (-6), OS detection (-O).
output: Port table with states, services, versions; XML/normal/grepable outputs.
example: Scan your own lab VM and compare -sS vs -sT results.
mistakes: Scanning third parties; overly aggressive timing; misreading filtered as closed.
limits: Noisy; blocked by firewalls; OS detection needs privileged access.

name: Masscan
purpose: Extremely fast TCP port scanner using asynchronous transmission.
arch: C scanner with custom TCP stack; can scan large ranges quickly.
install: apt install masscan or build from https://github.com/robertdavidgraham/masscan
cmd: masscan 10.0.0.0/24 -p80,443 --rate 1000 (owned ranges only).
advanced: Banner grabbing, output to JSON/XML, exclusion lists.
output: Discovered open ports with banners.
example: Scan your own isolated lab network and compare speed to Nmap.
mistakes: Extreme noise; high risk on shared networks; easy to cause disruption.
limits: Requires careful rate limiting; no version detection; may overwhelm networks.

name: Netcat (nc)
purpose: Network utility for reading/writing data over TCP/UDP.
arch: Simple CLI using sockets; can listen, connect, and transfer files.
install: Usually preinstalled (ncat from Nmap is an alternative).
cmd: nc -lvnp 4444 (listen); nc host 80 (connect).
advanced: Reverse/bind shells in labs, file transfer, banner grabbing, port checks.
output: Raw stream output in terminal.
example: Use nc to request a file from a local lab server and capture the response.
mistakes: Using it for unauthorized access; leaving listeners open.
limits: No encryption; no authentication; raw and error-prone.

name: Amass
purpose: Attack surface mapping and subdomain discovery.
arch: Go tool with configurable data sources and a graph data model.
cmd: amass enum -passive -d example.com -o subs.txt.
advanced: Active enumeration, API integrations, data source configuration in YAML.
output: Subdomain lists, JSON, graphDB outputs.
example: Enumerate subdomains of a domain you own; compare passive vs active (authorized) results.
mistakes: API keys needed for full coverage; active mode can be noisy and out of scope.
limits: Data source availability changes; rate limits on free APIs.

name: Subfinder
purpose: Fast passive subdomain discovery.
arch: Go tool with many passive source modules; configurable providers.
cmd: subfinder -d example.com -o subs.txt.
advanced: Multiple resolvers, sources config, JSON output, rate limiting.
output: One subdomain per line; deduplicated.
example: Enumerate your own domain and deduplicate against CT log results.
mistakes: Assuming results are complete; using it on out-of-scope domains.
limits: Passive only; source coverage varies.

name: Assetfinder
purpose: Find domains/subdomains related to a target using public sources.
arch: Go tool querying certificate transparency and other public datasets.
cmd: assetfinder --subs-only example.com > subs.txt.
advanced: Combine with httpx/dnsx in pipelines.
output: Plain list of domains.
example: Compare with subfinder output for a domain you own.
mistakes: Public data only; may include unrelated domains.
limits: Limited sources; no validation of liveness.

name: httpx
purpose: Fast HTTP toolkit for probing live hosts and extracting metadata.
arch: Go tool with concurrent requests and configurable probes.
cmd: httpx -l subs.txt -status-code -title -tech-detect -o live.txt.
advanced: Probe paths, custom headers, TLS info, rate limiting, JSON output.
output: Each line: URL, status, title, tech, content length.
example: Probe a list of your own subdomains and sort by status code.
mistakes: High concurrency against unauthorized targets; ignoring rate limits.
limits: Only probes; does not exploit.

name: dnsx
purpose: Fast DNS toolkit for querying and filtering DNS data.
arch: Go tool using configurable resolvers and question types.
cmd: dnsx -l subs.txt -a -cname -resp -o dns.txt.
advanced: Wildcard filtering, custom resolvers, JSON, extract records.
output: Resolved records per host.
example: Resolve your own subdomains and identify wildcard DNS behavior.
mistakes: Using unreliable public resolvers; misinterpreting NXDOMAIN.
limits: DNS only; no HTTP validation.

name: Nuclei
purpose: Template-based vulnerability scanner with a large community template library.
arch: Go engine executing YAML templates for HTTP, DNS, TCP, and more.
cmd: nuclei -u https://target -t templates/ (authorized targets only).
advanced: Custom templates, severity filtering, OOB via interactsh, rate limiting.
output: Findings with template ID, severity, matched request/response.
example: Write a simple template that checks for a header on your own lab server.
mistakes: Running all templates without scope; high request volume; false positives.
limits: Template quality varies; not a replacement for manual testing.

name: Katana
purpose: Web crawler that discovers endpoints, including from JavaScript.
arch: Go crawler with headless browser support for JS-heavy apps.
cmd: katana -u https://target -o urls.txt (authorized).
advanced: Headless mode (-headless), scope control, custom headers, form filling.
output: Crawled URLs and discovered endpoints.
example: Crawl your own SPA and list endpoints only discoverable via JS.
mistakes: Over-crawling; hitting logout or state-changing links; missing auth context.
limits: Can be noisy; may miss client-side routes.

name: Waybackurls
purpose: Retrieves historical URLs from the Wayback Machine.
arch: Go CLI querying the Internet Archive CDX API.
cmd: echo example.com | waybackurls > old.txt.
advanced: Combine with filters to extract parameters and file extensions.
output: One historical URL per line.
example: Collect historical URLs for your own domain and find forgotten endpoints.
mistakes: Archived endpoints may be dead; archive API rate limits.
limits: Depends on archive coverage; stale data.

name: Gau (GetAllURLs)
purpose: Fetches known URLs from multiple passive sources.
arch: Go tool querying Wayback, Common Crawl, and other datasets.
cmd: gau example.com > urls.txt.
advanced: Filter by extension/status; combine with httpx.
output: URL list from passive sources.
example: Compare gau and waybackurls output for a domain you own.
mistakes: Stale URLs; not validation of current existence.
limits: Passive only; source coverage varies.

name: Feroxbuster
purpose: Recursive content discovery (directories/files).
arch: Rust tool with recursion, filters, and wildcard detection.
cmd: feroxbuster -u https://target -w wordlist.txt (authorized).
advanced: Auto-filtering 404s, recursion depth, rate limits, proxy support.
output: Discovered paths with status, size, and response time.
example: Discover hidden directories on a local DVWA instance.
mistakes: High volume; scanning out of scope; recursive blow-up.
limits: Noisy; false positives with catch-all responses.

name: ffuf
purpose: Fast web fuzzer for paths, parameters, hosts, and values.
arch: Go fuzzer with keyword substitution (FUZZ) and rich filters/matchers.
cmd: ffuf -u https://target/FUZZ -w wordlist.txt -mc 200,301.
advanced: Multiple keyword positions, recursive mode, filter by size/time, JSON output.
output: Matched requests with status/size/time.
example: Fuzz a parameter name on your own lab app and inspect interesting sizes.
mistakes: Unbounded speed; hitting state-changing endpoints; ignoring rate limits.
limits: Requires careful filter tuning; noisy.

name: Gobuster
purpose: Directory, DNS, and vhost brute-forcing tool.
arch: Go tool with separate modes (dir, dns, vhost) and wordlist support.
install: apt install gobuster or go install github.com/OJ/gobuster/v3@latest
cmd: gobuster dir -u https://target -w wordlist.txt.
advanced: TLS, extensions, status filtering, vhost and dns modes.
output: Discovered names with status codes.
example: Enumerate vhosts on your own lab server.
mistakes: Scanning without authorization; default wordlists cause noise.
limits: Simpler than ffuf; no recursive crawling by default.

name: WhatWeb
purpose: Web technology fingerprinting tool.
arch: Ruby tool with plugins matching headers, HTML, cookies, and hashes.
cmd: whatweb https://target -v.
advanced: Aggression levels, plugin selection, JSON/XML output.
output: Identified technologies with confidence levels.
example: Fingerprint your own lab stack and verify findings against headers.
mistakes: Fingerprints can be spoofed; treat as hints, not proof.
limits: Plugin-based; may miss custom stacks.

name: Wappalyzer
purpose: Browser extension / service for technology detection.
arch: Browser extension with detection rules for frameworks, analytics, and server tech.
install: Install from official browser store or https://www.wappalyzer.com/
cmd: Browse to a site you own; view detected technologies in the extension.
advanced: Historical tech data; API for bulk lookups.
output: Panel listing detected technologies and versions.
example: Verify the framework used by your own lab app.
mistakes: Passive only; version guesses may be wrong.
limits: Limited to detectable signatures; API is paid for heavy use.

name: Shodan
purpose: Internet-wide search engine for exposed devices and services.
arch: Search platform with crawlers, banners, and filters; web UI and API.
cmd: Search by org, ASN, IP, or banner: org:"Example" port:443.
advanced: Filters for country, product, CVE, certificates; API automation.
output: Host records with banners, ports, location, and timestamps.
example: Find internet-facing assets belonging to an organization you are authorized to assess.
mistakes: Data may be stale; ownership must be verified before testing.
limits: Not live; cannot replace authorized active scans.

name: Censys
purpose: Internet-wide search and asset discovery platform.
arch: Search platform indexing certificates, hosts, and protocols with API access.
cmd: Search by certificate fingerprint, ASN, or organization.
advanced: Certificate search, host inventory, API for automation.
output: Host and certificate records with metadata.
example: Enumerate certificates for a domain you own and compare with CT logs.
mistakes: Free tier limits; verify ownership of discovered assets.
limits: Data freshness varies; passive only.

name: SecurityTrails
purpose: DNS and domain intelligence platform.
arch: Passive DNS database with historical records and API.
cmd: Look up a domain; view current/historical DNS records and subdomains.
advanced: DNS history, associated domains, WHOIS, API.
output: Subdomain lists and record timelines.
example: Review DNS history for your own domain to find forgotten subdomains.
mistakes: Historical data may include records you do not control.
limits: paid tiers for full data.

name: Semgrep
purpose: Lightweight static analysis using pattern rules across many languages.
arch: OCaml engine with YAML rules; local and CI modes; semgrep registry.
cmd: semgrep --config p/owasp-top-ten .
advanced: Custom rules, taint mode, autofix, CI integration.
output: Findings with file, line, rule ID, and severity.
example: Write a rule that flags string-concatenated SQL in a lab repo.
mistakes: Rule tuning needed; false positives.
limits: Not a full dataflow engine (unless using taint/pro rules).

name: CodeQL
purpose: Semantic code analysis engine that treats code as a queryable database.
arch: Builds a database from source; queries in QL; dataflow/taint analysis.
install: CLI via https://codeql.github.com/ ; GitHub Advanced Security integration.
cmd: codeql database create db --language=python; codeql database analyze db query.ql.
advanced: Custom queries, taint tracking, path queries showing data flow.
output: Alerts with source-to-sink paths.
example: Use a standard query to find injection sinks in a lab codebase.
mistakes: Steep learning curve for QL; database build can be slow.
limits: Requires build setup; complex for beginners.

name: Gitleaks
purpose: Secret scanning for git repositories and files.
arch: Go tool with regex/entropy rules scanning history and working trees.
cmd: gitleaks detect --source . --report-path report.json.
advanced: Custom rules, baseline/allowlist, CI integration, scanning full history.
output: Findings with file, line, commit, and secret type.
example: Scan a lab repo containing a deliberate fake API key and verify detection.
mistakes: False positives on test data; never commit real secrets to begin with.
limits: Only finds detectable patterns; rotating leaked secrets is essential.

name: Trivy
purpose: Vulnerability and misconfiguration scanner for containers, filesystems, and repos.
arch: Go scanner using vulnerability DBs; scans images, IaC, SBOMs, secrets.
cmd: trivy image mylab:latest; trivy fs .; trivy config .
advanced: IaC scanning, SBOM generation, severity filters, JSON output.
output: Vulnerability tables with CVE IDs, severity, fixed versions.
example: Scan a vulnerable lab container image and review CVEs.
mistakes: DB freshness; many findings need triage.
limits: Requires database updates; false positives possible.

name: Grype
purpose: Vulnerability scanner for container images and filesystems.
arch: Go tool using Syft-generated SBOMs and vulnerability feeds.
cmd: grype mylab:latest; syft mylab:latest -o json | grype.
advanced: SBOM-based scanning, JSON output, severity filters.
output: CVE list with package and fixed version.
example: Compare Grype and Trivy results on the same lab image.
mistakes: Different DBs yield different results; verify with vendor advisories.
limits: Not a config scanner.

name: Checkov
purpose: Static analysis for infrastructure-as-code misconfigurations.
arch: Python tool with policies for Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes, Dockerfiles.
cmd: checkov -d ./terraform.
advanced: Custom policies, baseline suppression, graph checks, CI integration.
output: Passed/failed checks with resource and guideline IDs.
example: Scan a lab Terraform file for an open S3 bucket and verify the finding.
mistakes: Suppressing checks without fixing; policy drift.
limits: Static only; cannot verify runtime state.

name: OWASP Dependency-Check
purpose: Identifies known vulnerable dependencies in projects.
arch: Java tool matching package identifiers against NVD data; CLI, Maven, Jenkins plugins.
cmd: dependency-check.sh --scan ./project --out report.
advanced: NVD mirror, suppression files, multiple report formats.
output: HTML/JSON report with CVEs and confidence scores.
example: Scan a lab project with an old dependency and review reported CVEs.
mistakes: NVD rate limits; false positives from package name matching.
limits: Slow first run (DB download); confidence tuning needed.

name: Browser Developer Tools
purpose: Built-in browser tools for inspecting DOM, network, storage, and scripts.
arch: Chrome/DevTools or Firefox Developer Tools with Elements, Network, Console, Sources, Application panels.
cmd: F12; Network tab to inspect requests; Application tab to inspect cookies/storage.
advanced: Breakpoints, request blocking, local overrides, performance profiling.
output: Request/response details, DOM tree, console errors, stored data.
example: Inspect a lab app's network requests to find the API endpoint used by a form.
mistakes: Leaving breakpoints/overrides active; inspecting real sessions carelessly.
limits: Browser-specific; cannot capture non-browser traffic.

name: Retire.js
purpose: Detects outdated JavaScript libraries with known vulnerabilities.
arch: CLI and browser extension scanning files/pages against a vulnerability DB.
cmd: retire --path ./public or scan a lab URL via extension.
advanced: CI integration, JSON output, package version detection from file hashes.
output: List of vulnerable libraries and referenced CVEs.
example: Scan your own site's JS bundles for outdated jQuery.
mistakes: Version detection can be fooled by minification/modification.
limits: Only known library vulnerabilities.

name: JWT.io
purpose: Online tool for decoding and inspecting JSON Web Tokens.
arch: Web debugger with Base64 decoding and signature verification against provided keys.
cmd: Paste a token from your own lab to inspect header and payload.
advanced: Verify with a secret/public key; library links for implementation.
output: Decoded header/payload JSON and signature status.
example: Decode a lab JWT and identify alg, exp, and aud fields.
mistakes: Pasting production tokens into a third-party site --- never do this.
limits: Decoding is not validation; browser tool only.

name: CyberChef
purpose: Browser-based data transformation and analysis tool.
arch: Client-side web app with composable operations (encode/decode, crypto, compression).
cmd: Drag operations: From Base64 -> URL Decode -> JSON Beautify.
advanced: Hundreds of operations; recipes can be saved and shared.
output: Transformed output in the output pane.
example: Decode a Base64-encoded lab cookie and inspect its contents.
mistakes: Pasting sensitive real data into a web tool; use self-hosted for sensitive work.
limits: Browser memory; not for secrets.

name: testssl.sh
purpose: Comprehensive TLS/SSL configuration testing.
arch: Bash script using OpenSSL to test protocols, ciphers, certs, and vulnerabilities.
cmd: testssl.sh https://your-lab-site.
advanced: Parallel testing, JSON/CSV output, check for specific issues.
output: Color-coded findings with severity and details.
example: Test TLS on a site you own and review cipher and header results.
mistakes: Testing third-party sites without permission may be noisy.
limits: Requires network access; results need expert interpretation.

name: Ghidra
purpose: Software reverse engineering suite with disassembly and decompilation.
arch: Java-based GUI with disassembler, decompiler, scripting, and collaboration features.
cmd: Create project, import binary, run Auto Analysis, view Decompiler window.
advanced: Headless analyzeHeadless, Python/Java scripts, function identification.
output: Disassembly listing and decompiled C-like pseudocode.
example: Load a small lab binary you compiled and locate main().
mistakes: Misreading decompiler output as ground truth; analyzing unauthorized binaries.
limits: Steep learning curve; decompilation is approximate.

name: IDA Free
purpose: Disassembler and debugger for binary analysis (free version has limits).
arch: Interactive disassembler with Hex-Rays decompiler available in paid versions.
cmd: Open a lab binary; navigate functions; view disassembly and graphs.
advanced: Debugger, plugins, IDAPython (paid feature set varies).
output: Disassembly with names, xrefs, and control-flow graphs.
example: Disassemble a lab C program and identify function boundaries.
mistakes: Assuming the free version has full decompiler; license restrictions.
limits: Free version lacks some architectures/decompiler.

name: radare2 / rizin
purpose: Open-source reverse engineering framework with CLI tools.
arch: Modular framework with disassembler, debugger, binary patching, and scripting.
install: Install via package manager or https://rada.re/
cmd: r2 -A ./labbin; then aaa; afl; pdf@main.
advanced: Visual mode (V), scripting, emulation, binary diffing.
output: Disassembly and analysis output in terminal.
example: Open a lab binary and list functions with afl.
mistakes: Command syntax has a steep learning curve; misusing write commands.
limits: Less polished UI than Ghidra.

name: GDB
purpose: GNU debugger for dynamic analysis of native programs.
arch: C debugger with breakpoints, stepping, memory/registers inspection, and scripting.
install: apt install gdb or via distro package manager.
cmd: gdb ./labbin; break main; run; info registers; x/20gx $rsp.
advanced: Conditional breakpoints, watchpoints, Python scripting, core dump analysis.
output: Register/memory dumps, stack traces, disassembly.
example: Set a breakpoint at a lab function and inspect stack memory.
mistakes: Debugging unfamiliar binaries without isolation; running untrusted code natively.
limits: Text UI; requires symbols for readable output.

name: Frida
purpose: Dynamic instrumentation toolkit for injecting scripts into running processes.
arch: JavaScript instrumentation via an injected agent; supports native and managed code.
cmd: frida -U -f com.lab.app -l script.js (rooted/jailbroken lab device or emulator).
advanced: Hooking functions, modifying return values, tracing, Stalker for code tracing.
output: Console logs from hooks and intercepted calls.
example: In a lab app, hook a method and log its arguments.
mistakes: Using on non-owned devices/apps; making apps behave unexpectedly.
limits: Requires compatible device/setup; detection by apps is common.

name: MobSF
purpose: Mobile Security Framework for automated static and dynamic analysis of apps.
arch: Django web app with static analyzers, dynamic analysis (via emulator), and reporting.
cmd: Start MobSF, upload an APK/IPA you own, view static report.
advanced: Dynamic analysis with emulator, API fuzzing, compare reports.
output: Report with permissions, manifest issues, hardcoded secrets, and findings.
example: Scan a lab APK and identify insecure storage findings.
mistakes: Scanning apps you do not own; treating automated findings as proof.
limits: Dynamic analysis needs a configured emulator; false positives.

name: JADX
purpose: Dex-to-Java decompiler for Android applications.
arch: Java tool decompiling APK/DEX to readable Java source with a GUI and CLI.
cmd: jadx -d out app.apk (open a lab APK you own).
advanced: Deobfuscation helpers, search, cross-references.
output: Decompiled Java source in output directory or GUI.
example: Decompile a lab APK and locate a hardcoded API endpoint.
mistakes: Decompiled code may be obfuscated/inaccurate.
limits: Functions names may be stripped; not all code is recoverable.

name: APKTool
purpose: Tool for decoding and rebuilding Android APK resources.
arch: Java tool decoding resources and manifest; rebuilds modified APKs.
cmd: apktool d app.apk; apktool b app -o rebuilt.apk.
advanced: Resource decoding, smali editing, framework support.
output: Decoded manifest, resources, and smali code.
example: Decode a lab APK and inspect AndroidManifest.xml permissions.
mistakes: Rebuilding and signing apps without understanding the process.
limits: Only handles Android resources; code is smali, not Java.

name: Objection
purpose: Runtime mobile security tool built on Frida.
arch: REPL and scripts built on Frida for Android/iOS runtime manipulation.
cmd: objection -g com.lab.app explore; then android keystore list.
advanced: SSL pinning bypass scripts, memory operations, intent launch.
output: Interactive REPL with command output.
example: In a lab app, use objection to inspect stored preferences.
mistakes: Requires a supported rooted/jailbroken or patched environment.
limits: App-specific; may be detected.

name: Android Studio Emulator
purpose: Official Android emulator for running apps in a controlled virtual device.
arch: QEMU-based virtual devices with Android system images; AVD manager.
cmd: Create an AVD; install a lab APK via adb install app.apk.
advanced: Rooted images, snapshots, network configuration, Google Play variants.
output: Emulator window and adb shell access.
example: Install a lab APK and inspect its network traffic via a proxy.
mistakes: Resource-heavy; snapshots may retain sensitive state.
limits: Emulation may not reflect real device behavior.

name: Prowler
purpose: Open-source cloud security auditing and benchmarking tool.
arch: Python tool calling cloud provider APIs to run compliance checks (AWS, Azure, GCP).
cmd: prowler aws --region us-east-1 (only on accounts you own/are authorized).
advanced: Compliance frameworks, multi-account, output to JSON/CSV, custom checks.
output: Pass/fail findings with severity and resource IDs.
example: Audit your own lab AWS account for public S3 buckets.
mistakes: Requires credentials; scanning accounts you do not own is prohibited.
limits: Point-in-time; permissions needed for full coverage.

name: ScoutSuite
purpose: Multi-cloud security auditing tool producing an HTML report.
arch: Python tool reading cloud APIs to build an attack-surface report.
cmd: scout aws --profile labprofile (authorized accounts only).
advanced: Multiple providers, rule packs, detailed HTML dashboard.
output: HTML report with findings by service.
example: Audit a lab cloud account and review IAM findings.
mistakes: Requires read credentials; can be slow.
limits: Read-only; not a remediation tool.

name: CloudMapper
purpose: Tool for visualizing AWS environments and analyzing configuration.
arch: Python tool generating network diagrams from AWS API data.
cmd: Collect account data, then generate an interactive HTML map.
advanced: Find public IPs, IAM specifics, and trust relationships visually.
output: HTML visualization of VPCs, instances, and connections.
example: Map your own lab AWS environment and identify public exposure.
mistakes: Requires AWS credentials; only for owned/authorized accounts.
limits: AWS-focused; static snapshot.
